title: Opal Health - incident postmortem follow-up
summary: Follow-up on the 2027-10-30 production degradation. Reviewed root cause (cache eviction + rollout mismatch), mitigation steps taken, proposed reliability improvements (autoscaling tweaks, fallback policy, enhanced traces), and agreed next steps for benchmarks and customer-runbook updates.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Luis Moreno (Redwood CSM); Maya Chen (Opal Head of Platform), Ethan Ross (Opal SRE), Priya Anand (Opal Security), Samir Iqbal (Opal Dev Lead)

Summary (auto): postmortem follow-up after 2027-10-30 production slowdown. We will cover what we observed, immediate mitigations, and the plan to prevent recurrence.

[00:00] Jordan: Okay great thanks everyone for jumping on, um we'll keep this tight — 30, 35 minutes. We wanted to go over the timeline from last week, what priya and the team ran for mitigations, and, uh, the follow-up items. Maya, Ethan, do you want to start with a quick overview from your side?

[00:18] Maya: Sure, thanks Jordan. Briefly — last Friday (10/30) we saw a spike in tail latency across a couple of inference routes. It began around 08:40 our time, and sustained elevated p95/p99 for about 40 minutes. Our users saw slow responses and some retries. We did a manual rollback to the previous model variant and that helped but we want to understand root cause and get formal runbook updates.

[00:41] Ethan: Yeah, and just to add, during the event we noticed memory pressure on the edge nodes - KV cache eviction seemed to be thrashing, and some requests were falling back to cold starts. The first mitigation was disabling the new cache warming policy and then we scaled up a burst pool which brought latency back to normal.

[01:02] Priya K (Redwood SE): Right — from our telemetry the sequence looks like this: rollout of model variant v2.1 at ~08:30, concurrent change in cache warming config (alpha flag), then a GC cycle on a subset of services causing cache eviction across pods. When the cache was cold, request batching ended up longer because more tokens were recomputed. That increased CPU and caused backpressure to the autoscaler.

[01:28] Samir (Opal): There was also a mis-match between the rollout policy and your routing policy, so a small % of high-throughput routes got directed to nodes not in the dedicated burst pool, which amplified the impact.

[01:45] Jordan: A lot there, yeah. Priya can you confirm whether the cache eviction was due to config or actual memory leak? I think your earlier note said eviction happened because of smaller threshold, not a leak?

[02:00] Priya K: Correct — we don't see evidence of a mem leak in the heap dumps we captured. The eviction was triggered because the warming policy reduced reserved cache space during the rollout, and then the GC cadence on that node overlapped with heavy request load — leading to synchronous eviction. So it's a config + timing issue more than a leak.

[02:20] Ethan: The confusing part was the tracing — some spans were missing, probably due to a broken sidecar on one host. Traces didn't stitch cleanly which made it slow to debug in the moment.

[02:34] Maya: From our side we need clearer alerts for cache hit-rate and eviction rate, plus a runbook step for immediate rollback.

[02:45] Priya K: Totally agree. That's in our proposed mitigations: (1) add eviction-rate alerts, (2) pin cache reservation during rollouts, (3) default to warm cache population for critical routes, and (4) add a fallback model variant with smaller context windows that can serve when cache cold.

[03:10] Priya A (Opal Security): We also want to make sure any additional logging or traces don't include PHI. We are in healthcare and need to maintain compliance; can you confirm the traces are scrubbed and logs are KMS-encrypted at rest?

[03:24] Jordan: Yes on encryption at rest — we use customer-managed KMS for Private deployments, and for hosted we can optionally send logs to your SIEM. Priya K, do we have a short doc on redaction?

[03:35] Priya K: I have a draft docs link — I'll send. We do have PII/PHI redaction filters, but we need to show Opal how the sample logs look. We'll share the scrubbed snippets.

[03:48] Ethan: One operational question — during the incident we saw our autoscaler scale in too slowly for small short bursts. Could you explain how your burst pool scaling works?

[04:02] Priya K: Sure: our burst pool uses a buffer-based policy — it scales based on target concurrency and observed queue length, but it has cooldowns to avoid flapping. In this case the cooldown prevented immediate scaleup because the system was reacting to perceived prolonged load rather than a microspike. We're proposing to adjust cooldown parameters and allow a fast-path for routes marked critical.

[04:24] Samir: That fast-path would help. Also we need an explicit canary gating for any cache or warming policy changes — we don't want these flags to hit production-wide at once.

[04:35] Jordan: Agreed. Proposed short-term mitigations you accepted in the postmortem doc were: revert warming policy flag to previous defaults during rollouts, add eviction-rate alerts, and create a dedicated canary pool for cache-related flags. Any objections?

[04:51] Maya: No objections. We want timelines though — when can each mitigation be in place?

[04:58] Priya K: We can push the alert rule within 48 hours, the flag revert is immediate and already done for critical routes, and the canary pool we can enable as a config change in our next deploy — estimate by 2027-11-09.

[05:18] Ethan: For the canary pool, will it be auto-created or do we need to allocate capacity on our side?

[05:26] Priya K: For Hosted customers we create the pool — for Dedicated you have to allocate via the console. Opal is on Dedicated, correct?

[05:33] Maya: Yes Dedicated. So we'll need a capacity change request. Jordan, can you send the capacity delta and pricing?

[05:39] Jordan: Yep I'll send a brief addendum with numbers and the SLA change. Expect that by Friday (2027-11-05).

[05:50] Luis M (CSM): Also we'll run a joint benchmark next week (we propose Nov 9) to validate the fixes end-to-end. Priya K will own the Redwood side tests, Ethan will run the request patterns from Opal.

[06:06] Priya K: I'll prepare the KV-cache benchmark harness and a spreadsheet with results and raw logs attached. That will include hit-rate, eviction rate, tail latency per route, and memory usage.

[06:20] Maya: Good, please include per-region breakdowns — we saw the issue more pronounced in eu-west due to older host images.

[06:29] Priya K: Noted. We'll include eu-west and us-east comparisons.

[06:34] Priya A (Security): I need to loop in our compliance team. Two asks: can Redwood provide a scoped SOC2 audit extract for the last quarter and a list of who had access to traces during the incident? Also, explain how rollback artifacts are stored (S3 w/ KMS?).

[06:52] Jordan: Yes, we can provide the SOC2 extract for production and an access log for the incident window. Rollback artifacts are stored in an encrypted S3 bucket with customer-managed KMS keys for Private deployments; for Hosted we use our KMS but can feed artifacts to customer S3 if requested.

[07:10] Ethan: For the runbook, our ops team needs a clear step: detection -> triage -> revert flag -> scale burst pool -> notify engineers. Can we get a one-page playbook?

[07:22] Luis M: We'll prepare a one-page runbook and attach escalation contacts. Maya, we'll send a draft by 2027-11-05.

[07:31] Samir: Thinking longer term — what product changes are we discussing to make this less likely? You mentioned fallback model variants and pinning cache reservations. Anything else?

[07:43] Priya K: Roadmap-level items: 1) better per-route cache reservation controls, 2) faster autoscaler fast-path for critical routes, 3) model-variant compatibility checking before rollouts (we run a dry-run that simulates cache usage), 4) improved trace stitching and sampling to avoid missing spans. Some of these are short-term, some mid-term.

[08:01] Maya: The compatibility check sounds useful — can it detect if a variant will increase working set beyond your existing cache?

[08:09] Priya K: Yes — we estimate working set by simulating common prompts and compute estimated KV size. The dry-run compares expected working set against reserved cache. If it exceeds threshold, rollout is blocked until a reservation is increased or the model is changed.

[08:27] Ethan: One more ask — when you run benchmarks, please expose raw traces (scrubbed) because we found earlier that the aggregated metrics hid the short tail spikes.

[08:36] Priya K: We will provide scrubbed traces; we'll also deliver full p95/p99 distributions per route.

[08:44] Jordan: Okay sounds good. Quick check on timeline and owners: Priya K — KV benchmark + logs by Nov 9; Jordan — SLA/pricing addendum by Nov 5; Luis — runbook draft by Nov 5 and schedule workshop; Maya — review runbook by Nov 12. Does that match?

[09:02] Maya: Yes. Also two smaller items: can you confirm whether the canary gating will be UI driven via the console so Opal SREs can kick off canaries, or will it be API only?

[09:12] Priya K: Initially API-only but we can toggle a console feature flag; I'll add it to the request for the canary pool.

[09:21] Priya A (Security): And encryption of traces in transit — we need TLS v1.2+ and mutual TLS for any debug endpoints.

[09:29] Jordan: We support mTLS for debug endpoints and TLS 1.3 for public endpoints. We'll capture the security controls in the artifact that Priya K sends.

[09:40] Ethan: One small note — some names in the logs were redacted oddly, e.g., 'K V cache' showing as 'kay vee' in speech transcription, so when you share the log samples, please include both machine and human readable context.

[09:52] Priya K: Will do.

[10:00] Jordan: Anything else from the Opal team?

[10:03] Samir: Not from me. We'll wait for the benchmark. Also I'd like a short called-out section in the runbook about escalation to legal/compliance if there is PHI exposure — even if it's hypothetical.

[10:14] Priya A: I'll work with Maya to draft that language and share.

[10:20] Jordan: Great. We'll recap action items in email. Thanks everyone for concise updates. We'll check back after the benchmark and runbook are shared.

[10:29] Luis M: Thanks all.

[10:31] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms (KV as 'kay vee'), missing spans in tracing language, some filler words and overlaps.

- Runbook draft (will be attached): https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/opal-cache-incident
